title: Crypto funds rebound with $1B inflows after five-week slump
summary: Crypto ETPs saw $1 billion in inflows last week, led by $787 million into US spot Bitcoin ETFs, ending a five-week outflow streak of nearly $4 billion

title: Sony Bank and JPYC to test instant yen stablecoin buys from customer accounts
summary: Sony Bank and JPYC will study real-time transfers enabling customers to buy the yen-pegged stablecoin JPYC directly from their bank accounts.

title: Hong Kong, Shanghai authorities to test blockchain for cargo trade data
summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Shanghai partners will study a blockchain cross-border platform linking cargo trade data, e-bills of lading and finance under Project Ensemble.

title: ‘This is not World War III:’ Five things to know in Bitcoin this week
summary: Bitcoin avoided an Iran sell-off to start March, but traders still expected BTC price support to give way in bearish market conditions.

title: European banks seek exchange partners ahead of 2026 stablecoin launch
summary: Qivalis, a European banking consortium, is reportedly in talks with crypto exchanges ahead of a planned euro stablecoin launch in the second half of 2026.

title: Aave proposal clears first hurdle with 52.6% support amid governance split
summary: Tokenholders backed a $42.5 million stablecoin package and 75,000 AAVE allocation for Aave Labs under a proposed DAO-funded revenue model.

title: South Korea orders cross-agency probe after repeated crypto custody failures
summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-cheol ordered an inter-agency review of seized crypto wallets after the National Tax Service exposed a seed phrase in a press release.

title: Bitcoin to see tailwinds if AI prompts ‘easier monetary policy’: NYDIG
summary: NYDIG’s Greg Cipolaro says AI could be a “general-purpose technology,” and its effects on the economy could be a boon for Bitcoin.

title: Fed could print money to support US conflict with Iran, says Hayes
summary: Arthur Hayes says the longer Donald Trump engages in expensive “Iranian nation-building,” the more likely it is that the Federal Reserve will boost money supply.

title: February crypto losses hit lowest level since March 2025, says PeckShield
summary: PeckShield said fewer mega-hacks, heightened volatility and tighter risk controls may have helped push crypto losses to their lowest level in 11 months.
